Summary: The guide outlines the steps to create a simple zero waste tunic using a single pattern piece and various editing tools. Here’s a comprehensive breakdown of the process: 1. **Setting Up the Fabric**: - Change the default fabric to muslin for the initial pattern. 2. **Creating the Pattern Piece**: - Use the rectangle tool to draw a rectangular pattern piece measuring 24 inches wide by 48 inches high. 3. **Editing the Pattern**: - Select the edit pattern tool to unfold the pattern symmetrically along the center line. - Offset an internal line 10.5 inches down from the top, then add another line 1.25 inches below that. 4. **Adding Points**: - On the first internal line, use the add point split line tool to insert a point 3 inches from the center line. - Right-click on that point and choose "divide internal point". 5. **Deleting Sections**: - With the edit pattern tool, select the longer section of the newly divided line and delete it. - On the second internal line, measure 12.5 inches from the side, right-click, and choose "cut" to create a split. 6. **Drawing Additional Lines**: - Add a point 12.5 inches from the side at the top of the pattern. - Where the first internal line crosses the center, draw a 6-inch vertical line downwards. - Connect the top of this vertical line to the bottom of the 6-inch line with a horizontal line. 7. **Merging Points**: - Use the edit pattern tool to mark and merge points where the horizontal and angled lines intersect. - Right-click on the pattern and choose "remove linked editing" to make independent edits. 8. **Finalizing the Triangle Shape**: - Delete the two internal lines inside the triangle formed due to symmetrical cutting. - Use the merge to point technique to connect any unjoined segment points. - Select the entire triangle shape, cut it, and move it aside in the 2D window (do not delete it for zero waste purposes). 9. **Creating Cuts for Assembly**: - Draw an internal line from the top center of the pattern down to the top of the triangle and perform a cut. - Simulate the pattern in the 3D view to observe draping. 10. **Adjusting the Avatar**: - Turn on X-ray joints for the avatar and adjust the arms to achieve a T-pose. - Rotate the pattern in the 3D window to position the neck opening correctly. 11. **Simulating and Final Adjustments**: - Simulate the design to assess the drape and make adjustments using tools like strengthen and pins for alignment. - If desired, segment sew the center back together, utilizing the segment points added earlier for the arms and back. 12. **Recreating the Triangle**: - Zoom in on the triangle cutout, add segment points to its sides, and drag them to recreate the triangle shape. - Delete the initial triangle shape used for cutting. 13. **Final Touches**: - Simulate the tunic again, making additional adjustments such as enlarging the neck opening, adding internal lines for a folded collar, and lengthening the hem. - Optionally, add a pocket using leftover fabric and change the fabric to cotton gabardine with a stripe print. - Consider adding folded hems and top stitching for added detail. This guide provides a systematic approach to designing a zero waste tunic, emphasizing the importance of strategic cutting and pattern manipulation for efficient fabric use.
